book.title: Career and Technical Education Grade 7 Student Textbook
book.subject: cte

title: Definition of soft skills
competency: Describe soft skills and how they differ from hard skills.

keywords.def: Personal qualities that help you work well with others, do your job and grow in your career.
Skills specific to a certain type of task, like repairing a car.

en.text: Soft skills are personal qualities that help you work well with others, do your job well and grow in your career. They are called soft because they do not define one job, like repairing a car. Hard skills are specific to one kind of task. Soft skills are useful in almost every job.

screens.title: Useful everywhere
screens.ask: Which skill helps you in almost every job: listening well, or welding metal?
screens.after: Listening helps in every job. Welding helps in one kind of job. Listening is a soft skill.

screens.title: Brainstorming question
screens.ask: Can you identify skills that help build good interaction between people?
screens.answer: Examples: communication, listening, respect for others, good manners, teamwork, self-confidence.

screens.title: 2.2.1 Definition of soft skills
paras: Soft skills are general abilities that shape how you relate to others.
They improve your interactions, your job performance and your career chances.
They are called "soft" because they do not define someone's work, like repairing a car.

screens.title: Soft skills vs hard skills
paras: Soft skills can be used in any career.
Hard skills are specific to a certain type of task.
Soft skills are not job-specific. They are universal abilities everyone must develop.
table: Specific to one type of task

screens.title: Key words
defs: Personal qualities that help you work well with others, do your job and grow in your career.
Skills specific to a certain type of task, like repairing a car.

screens.text: Which one is a soft skill?
screens.why: Teamwork helps in any job. The others are job-specific hard skills.
screens.clue: Which one is useful in every job?

screens.why: Soft skills fit every job; hard skills fit one type of task.
screens.clue: Could a teacher, a farmer and a nurse all use it?

screens.text: Hard skills are universal while soft skills are specific to a job.
screens.why: It is the other way round. Soft skills are universal; hard skills are job-specific.

screens.text: ___ skill is specific for a certain job.
screens.why: Hard skills are specific to a type of task.
screens.clue: Problem solving and critical thinking are soft skills.

screens.text: "Sewing is a hard skill for a carpenter." What is wrong with this sentence?
opts: Sewing is a hard skill for a tailor, not a carpenter
screens.ans: Sewing is a hard skill for a tailor, not a carpenter
screens.why: Hard skills belong to a job. A carpenter cuts and shapes wood; sewing belongs to textile and garment work.

test.text: Repairing a car is a soft skill.
test.why: It is specific to one task, so it is a hard skill.

opts: They do not define one particular job
test.ans: They do not define one particular job
test.why: The book says they are not skills that define someone's work.

test.ask: Soft skills help your interactions, your job performance and your ___ prospects.
test.why: They enhance interactions, job performance and career prospects.

test.text: Kidist is an excellent mechanic but shouts at customers. Which skill should she build?
opts: Soft skills like communication and respect
test.ans: Soft skills like communication and respect
test.why: Her hard skill is strong; her interaction with people needs soft skills.
